sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Wnt5a-stimulated signalling (JNK/Rac1 pathway) and anti-Flag antibody-mediated receptor clustering both elicit downstream responses indistinguishable from untagged controls; receptor is surface-displayed and ligand-responsive.
sites.rationale: L4/L5 report N-terminal Flag-tagged full-length human Ror2 that is stably expressed, surface-accessible to anti-Flag antibody from outside the cell, and functionally responsive to Wnt5a. ROR2 has a signal peptide (residues 1–33) that is cleaved co-translationally; the only extracellular N-terminal junction is after residue 33 (G) and before residue 34 (E, the mature N-terminus). Python confirmed r(33)=G and r(34)=E. The tag is ≥370 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 404), providing ample space for a short epitope tag. Ror2−/− MEFs stably expressing N-terminal Flag-tagged full-length Ror2 (human); anti-Flag antibody applied extracellularly crosslinked and clustered the receptor, confirming the Flag tag is surface-exposed. Multiple lentiviral constructs (Ror2-S864A, Ror2-K507A, Ror2-S864D, Ror2-S864E) all carry the same N-terminal Flag. The paper names only 'N-terminal' with no residue number; with a signal peptide spanning 1–33 the sole valid extracellular N-terminal junction is after residue 33 (mature N-terminus = E34), computed from the topology landmarks.

literature_notes: All C-terminal fusions in the ledger (Ror2-mCherry L7, Ror2-GFP L8, zfRor2-mCherry L10, ROR2-mCherry ΔCRD L13) are intracellular because ROR2 is a type I single-pass receptor with its C-terminus in the cytoplasm (residues 426–943 intracellular per topology landmarks); these are recorded in other_positions. L1/L2/L3 (CFP-ROR2, YFP-ROR2, human, PMC10654037) and L8 (GFP-Ror2, zebrafish) and L9/L11 (mCherry-Ror2, zebrafish/Xenopus) all corroborate the same N-terminal extracellular junction (after residue 33) but L4 is the strongest single line (direct human, Flag, surface crosslinking + functional readout) and is used as the primary supporting clip. No ledger line reports a tag in any internal extracellular loop of ROR2 with a named residue or a named loop; no internal site is therefore proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: Ror2-mCherry (C-terminal mCherry fusion) is surface-displayed on cytonemes but the C-terminus of ROR2 is cytoplasmic (intracellular domain 426–943); the tag is intracellular, not a surface epitope site.
Ror2-GFP (C-terminal GFP fusion, zebrafish) is expressed and imaged on cytonemes but the C-terminus is cytoplasmic; intracellular tag only.
ROR2-mCherry ΔCRD (C-terminal mCherry on human ROR2 with CRD deletion R178–Y313) is used for FRET/functional studies; C-terminal position is intracellular.
